title: Capacity
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4; not yet checked by a Kenyan maths teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Outcomes a to c are KICD's words, with b read from the PDF where the text layer lost the fraction signs: 'litres and litres' in the table is half a litre and a quarter of a litre (the design's own competence text says half-litre and quarter-litre containers). To confirm by a person. Outcome d attitudinal. Millilitres are not in Grade 4. Hands-on measuring with containers is done in class.

skills.key_step: The child counts how many full 1 litre measures fill a container, reading the level the liquid reaches, not the top of the jug.

floor.question: How many 1 litre bottles fill a 5 litre jerrycan?

representations: a 1 litre bottle and a jerrycan
steps: Fill the litre measure to the line.
Pour and count each full litre.
Read a jug at the level of the water.
Height alone does not tell capacity.
contexts: a jerrycan of water from the borehole

board.do: Draw a 5 litre jug with water at the 3 mark.
Point at the top of the water.
board.say: How much water is in the jug?

misconceptions.ask: Do we pour or weigh water to see how much a can holds?
Where is the top of the water?
Was every pour a full litre?

checks.question: A jug is marked to 4 litres. The water is at the 2 mark. How much water?
How many 1 litre bottles fill a 10 litre bucket?

skills.key_step: The child knows 2 half litres and 4 quarter litres each make 1 litre.

floor.prerequisite: Halves and quarters of a whole.
floor.question: How many quarters make a whole?

steps: Pour half litres into a litre: 2 fill it.

board.do: Draw a 1 litre jug and a 1/4 litre cup.
Count the cups poured with the child: 1, 2, 3, 4.
Ask: how many half litres would fill it?

misconceptions.ask: How many halves make a whole?
How many quarters make a whole?
Is half a litre more or less than a litre?
How many quarter cups fill a half cup?

checks.question: How many 1/2 litre packets make 3 litres?
How many 1/4 litre cups make 2 litres?

skills.key_step: The child adds the litres in each container and writes the unit, carrying tens when needed.
steps: Write the litres in each container.
Halves and quarters: count how many make a litre.

board.do: Draw two jerrycans of 20 litres and a bucket of 10 litres.

board.say: How many litres does each hold?

misconceptions.ask: How many halves fill a litre?
Did I ask how many containers?

checks.question: A cow gives 9 litres in the morning and 7 litres in the evening. How much milk?

skills.key_step: The child takes the litres used from the litres there were and gives what is left, with the bigger amount first.
representations: a drum with a level line

board.do: Draw a 20 litre drum; shade 7 litres used.
Point at the part not shaded.

misconceptions.ask: Is there more or less after using some?
How much more fills the tank: take away or add?
Is 7 the water used or left?

checks.question: A tank holds 60 litres. 24 litres are used. How much is left?
A 25 litre jerrycan has 18 litres. How much more fills it?
